w11-q1: Incorrect — one-directional distribution describes the traditional grid, not the smart grid.
Incorrect — a smart grid automates monitoring and restoration, so they are not always performed manually.
Correct — a smart grid supports bidirectional energy flows with two-way communication and control.
Incorrect — a smart grid allows distributed generation, so generation is not restricted to centralized power plants.
w11-q2: Incorrect — a smart meter measures and communicates consumption; it does not generate electricity.
Correct — smart meters work digitally and provide the interface for information exchange between the consumer and the energy service provider.
Incorrect — a smart meter supplies data to energy management but does not replace the home energy management system.
Incorrect — a smart meter is two-way and exchanges information, unlike a conventional one-way meter.
w11-q3: Correct — Time-of-Use pricing encourages shifting consumption to off-peak periods, when grid load and energy price are lower.
Incorrect — on-peak hours have higher grid load and price, so operating appliances then raises cost.
Incorrect — Time-of-Use pricing is about price differences across the day, not about blackouts.
Incorrect — Time-of-Use pricing rewards shifting use according to grid load and price, not running at a fixed time.
w11-q4: Incorrect — reactive power and communication traffic do not determine a net metering bill.
Incorrect — net metering also counts energy the consumer supplies, so centralized plant output alone does not decide the bill.
Incorrect — stored battery energy alone does not determine the bill; the grid exchange does.
Correct — net-metering bills depend on energy received from the grid and excess energy the consumer supplies back to it.
w11-q5: Correct — a PMU samples voltage and current at its location, and multiple PMUs form a phasor network analyzed by SCADA.
Incorrect — a DAU collects data from groups of smart meters and is not the voltage and current sampling device.
Incorrect — a smart appliance controller manages appliances at the consumer side, not transmission system monitoring.
Incorrect — Universal Power Line Bus is a home power-line communication technology, not a grid monitoring device.
w11-q6: Incorrect — distribution intelligence relies on smart meters and smart IoT devices rather than preventing their use.
Correct — distribution intelligence identifies outage sources and supports automated switching and power-flow restoration.
Incorrect — the smart grid uses two-way communication, so restricting it to one-way is the opposite of the function.
Incorrect — distribution intelligence includes protecting and controlling feeder lines, not removing that protection.
w11-q7: Correct — a gateway connects a group of closely located smart meters and links them to the DAUs.
Incorrect — a gateway does not link power plants directly to home appliances.
Incorrect — PMUs are transmission monitoring devices and are not connected to plug-in vehicles by a gateway.
Incorrect — a gateway links a group of closely located smart meters to the DAUs, not renewable generators to SCADA.
w11-q8: Incorrect — net metering is a billing scheme, not a type of attack.
Incorrect — time synchronization attacks target timing information and are not the attack on availability.
Incorrect — data visualization attack is not the availability-compromising attack named in the lecture.
Correct — Denial of Service attacks compromise availability by making components or information inaccessible when needed.
w11-q9: Correct — IIoT applies IoT to industrial systems, linking automation with enterprise functions, planning and product lifecycle.
Incorrect — IIoT targets industrial settings, not consumer home entertainment.
Incorrect — IIoT builds on industrial automation by networking it, rather than replacing it without networking.
Incorrect — IIoT involves machine-to-machine communication as well as data handling, not storage alone.
w11-q10: Incorrect — disconnect and isolate would keep existing assets out of the network, the opposite of IIoT integration.
Incorrect — IIoT follows 'wrap and re-use' rather than 'rip and replace'.
Correct — IIoT is based on a 'wrap and re-use' approach, integrating existing industrial assets.
Incorrect — remove and discard is not the approach; IIoT aims to reuse existing industrial systems.
w11-q11: Incorrect — Universal Power Line Bus is a home power-line control technology, not a vehicular communication enabler.
Incorrect — HDFS is a big data storage file system, unrelated to V2V and V2R communication.
Incorrect — SCADA is an industrial supervisory and control system, not the vehicular communication technology.
Correct — DSRC is the key enabling technology for V2V and V2R communications in Intelligent Transportation Systems.
w11-q12: Correct — wireless sensor networks can monitor air quality, poisonous gases and oxygen levels for mining safety.
Incorrect — billing amounts of workers are not environmental parameters sensed in mines.
Incorrect — equipment color is not an environmental parameter and is not monitored for safety.
Incorrect — browsing history is not an environmental parameter and has no role in mining safety monitoring.
w11-q13: Incorrect — value refers to the worth that can be derived from data, not to its biases and noise.
Incorrect — variability refers to changes in data flow or meaning over time, not to noise and bias.
Correct — veracity concerns biases, noise and abnormality in data, which matters for automated decision-making and machine learning.
Incorrect — volume refers to the sheer amount of data, not its quality.
w11-q14: Incorrect — redundancy mitigation removes repeated data; it does not stop data collection.
Incorrect — duplicating items would add redundancy, which is the opposite of mitigation.
Incorrect — redundancy mitigation is unrelated to converting structured data into images.
Correct — redundancy mitigation eliminates repeated data through detection, filtering and compression, reducing needless transmission and storage.
w11-q15: Correct — Datanodes store the actual data blocks, which HDFS replicates across Datanodes.
Incorrect — the Namenode maintains filesystem metadata, not the data blocks themselves.
Incorrect — the Job Tracker schedules and tracks MapReduce jobs; it does not store HDFS blocks.
Incorrect — YARN manages cluster resources and does not store HDFS data blocks.
